lines.trans: There is a wall of chairs from the lemon pot all the way to the stairs!
Good news first: every single chair was fifty percent off!
And what is the bad news, Mazen?
I asked for six, agreed to twenty-four, and accidentally said "today"!

lines.trans: Oh! Four folded chairs take no more space than one suitcase!

lines.trans: Really? Show me that latch, Nour!

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of أكثر ('more, most').

examples.trans: I liked working here much more.
Who knows the neighbourhood better than you?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقذ, بينقذ).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
You saved my whole trip.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian for 12. From eleven up, the counted noun stays singular: اتنعش فنجان 'twelve cups'.

examples.trans: We have twelve guests tonight.
It's twelve noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رتّب ('to tidy, arrange'); بترتيب means 'neatly, in neat order'.

examples.trans: We lined the chairs up neatly beside the wall.

examples.text: ترتيب الطاولات بالساحة ما أخد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Arranging the tables in the courtyard did not take ten minutes.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Verbal noun of عيّن ('to appoint, hire to a post').

examples.text: فرحنا كتير بخبر تعيين نور بالنزل.
examples.trans: We were delighted at the news of Nour's permanent appointment at the inn.
The manager signed the appointment letter in the morning.

meanings.note: Relative adjective (nisba) from جانب ('side'), e.g. الباب الجانبي ('the side door'), القفل الجانبي ('the side latch').

examples.text: افتح الشباك الجانبي عشان يفوت الهوا.
examples.trans: Open the side window so fresh air comes in.

examples.text: في ممر جانبي صغير ورا المطبخ.
examples.trans: There is a small side passage behind the kitchen.

meanings.note: Means 'grandfather' (جدي my grandfather) and in عن جد ('really / seriously') means 'earnestness'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Life is sweet with kind people.
Never in my life have I seen a prettier view.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخبار.

examples.trans: I have good news for you today!
They have no news yet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خصومات.

examples.trans: We gave him a fifty-percent discount.
There is a special discount for weekly guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخلص, بيخلص).

examples.trans: I finished making the bed quickly!

examples.text: كل ما أخلص عزف كنا نحكي.
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, we used to chat.

meanings.note: Numeral 'fifty'.

examples.trans: Here is fifty dinars from the cash box.
She saved fifty piastres on the bill.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دائمة, plural: دائمين).

examples.trans: She became the permanent reception manager at the guesthouse.
He wrote it in the ledger in permanent ink.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برفع, بيرفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Numeral 'six'; short form ست (sitt) before a plural noun (ست سنين 'six years').

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: كتب السفر are travel books; على سفر means 'away travelling'.

examples.trans: I love travelling by bus.
My brother is away travelling this week.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Transitive verb meaning 'to lean or prop something upright against a wall or arch'.

examples.text: اسند السلم منيح عالحيط قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Prop the ladder firmly against the wall before climbing up.

examples.text: سندنا الكراسي المطوية تحت القوس الحجر.
examples.trans: We leaned the folded chairs under the stone arch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

شوي.gloss: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Classic Jordanian/Levantine opposite of منيح or حلو in الخبر الحلو والخبر العاطل ('the good news and the bad news').

examples.text: احكيلي الخبر الحلو قبل الخبر العاطل!
examples.trans: Tell me the good news before the bad news!

examples.text: الجو مش عاطل أبدا لتمشاية الصبح.
examples.trans: The weather is not bad at all for a morning walk.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Used as noun in بالغلط ('by mistake') and عالغلط ('for the mistake'), and invariable predicate 'wrong' (في شي غلط something is wrong).

examples.trans: He took the other suitcase by mistake.
Sorry for the mistake, my apologies.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine everyday verb for 'to show' (فرجيني 'show me!').

examples.trans: Show the shopkeeper this brass valve.
Let me show you my real work!

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فوقانية, plural: فوقانيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
The red ribbon is in the top pocket.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قفال.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper unlocked the padlock in the morning.
We fitted a new brass lock on the closet.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Levantine word (qawwaar, plural qawaawiir) for a clay courtyard plant pot.

examples.text: زرعنا نعنع أخضر بقواوير فخار بالساحة.
examples.trans: We planted green mint in clay pots in the courtyard.

examples.text: سقت نور قوار الليمون جنب الدرج.
examples.trans: Nour watered the lemon pot beside the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: The Amman verb for pressing a button, doorbell or switch.

examples.text: اكبس الزر الأحمر عشان يفتح الباب.
examples.trans: Press the red button to open the door.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرتين وما حدا فتح.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell twice and nobody opened.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كراسي.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Combines with ما before a verb to mean 'until' (لحد ما اتصلت 'until you called').

examples.trans: We waited until you called us.
I stayed up until midnight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لمبات.

examples.trans: I fitted a new bulb in the attic bathroom.
The white lightbulb is bright.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'one hundred' (مية مرة 'a hundred times' — construct مية miyyet before a noun).

examples.trans: Yes, a hundred times yes!
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمشي, بيمشي).

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.

examples.text: اسمع، المي عم بتمشي جوا الماسورة!
examples.trans: Listen, the water is flowing inside the pipe!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناشفة, plural: ناشفين).

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (ن-ط-ط) for jumping or hopping over an obstacle.

examples.text: القطة نطت عن الحيط للجنينة بهدوء.
examples.trans: The cat jumped quietly off the wall into the garden.

examples.text: ما بدنا الضيوف ينطوا فوق الكراسي بالممر!
examples.trans: We don't want guests climbing over chairs in the hallway!

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Form III verb from و-ف-ق; takes على for the thing agreed to.

examples.text: وافق مازن عالخطة أول ما شاف الأرقام.
examples.trans: Mazen agreed to the plan as soon as he saw the numbers.

examples.text: كل الجيران وافقوا يحضروا حفلة الشاي.
examples.trans: All the neighbours agreed to attend the tea concert.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
